fixes.explanation: Counted? Friend, I count everything. I once counted chocolate chips, lost track somewhere past forty, started over, and burned the batch. But no count happens here. Joshua 5:8 says they stayed in the camp until they were healed.

Bethel is a real place name, but it's not the one on this box. The LORD tells Joshua, “Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you.” Then the verse says, “So that place has been called Gilgal to this day.” (Joshua 5:9). Bethel showed up ready to work, but Gilgal got the job.

Shiloh has a nice ring, baker. It sounds like a name you'd paint on a bakery window. But the verse says, “So that place has been called Gilgal to this day.” (Joshua 5:9). Gilgal is the name that stuck, and it was still in use when the writer wrote.

Sabbath is a solid guess, but it never shows up in this passage. The verse hands you a date: the evening of the fourteenth day of the month. What the Israelites kept that evening was the Passover (Joshua 5:10). When the text gives you a date that specific, friend, it's doing half the work for you.

Purim is a festival that isn't in this story, baker. Joshua 5:10 says that on the evening of the fourteenth day, while camped at Gilgal, they kept the Passover. You were reaching for a holiday, and I respect the reach. My mustache stretches to the top shelf and still misses half the time.

The cloud is a big thing to guess, but it isn't in this passage. What ceased is the manna, the day after they ate from the produce of the land. “There was no more manna for the Israelites, so that year they began to eat the crops of the land of Canaan.” (Joshua 5:12). A cloud vanishing would be quite a plot twist, but this verse has a different one.
